name: Form
intent: One form: an optional title, kit fields (or titled sections of them) and the actions that save it.
usage: Use Form to wrap kit fields (Input, Textarea, Select, DatePicker, Lookup, Cascader, FormulaEditor, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch) that save together. Read-only values go in FormDisplay rows; back-to-back rows sit flush as one list. Pass the fields as children, or as sections when they fall into groups like Company and Billing; each section is a titled group. labelPosition="start" puts every field's label in a column at the beginning; columns={2} puts fields side by side. A long form of groups — a create page — takes sections with collapsible, and the save can sit outside the form: give the Form an id and the Button type="submit" with form set to it, so one press still saves one form. actions holds kit Buttons: secondary first, one primary last with type="submit". Enter in a field submits, and onSubmit gets the values by field name. Inside a Modal, skip the title (the Modal names it), give the Form an id, and put the Save Button in the Modal footer with form set to that id. See contracts/form.json for the full contract.

title.note: 18px heading. It names the form for screen readers. Skip it inside a Modal.

description.note: One line under the title. Read with the form.

variant.note: plain sits on the page. card is a bordered panel with a faint footer, like a settings block.

labelPosition.note: Where the kit fields inside put their label. start puts it in a 160px column at the beginning; Checkbox, Switch and RadioGroup line up with the fields. Under 480px the fields put their label back on top, since a label column would leave too little of the field. A field's own labelPosition still wins.

columns.note: 2 puts fields side by side, left to right; 3 puts them in threes, for a long form on a wide page. A Textarea spans the row. Columns give way as the form narrows: three become two under 720px (1080px with start labels), and two become one under 560px (720px with start labels).

children.note: The kit fields, top to bottom. Use this or sections, not both.

sections.itemShape: { title: string; description?: string; help?: string; actions?: ReactNode; content: ReactNode; line?: "medium" | "thin"; collapsible?: boolean; expanded?: boolean; defaultExpanded?: boolean; onExpandedChange?: (expanded: boolean) => void }
sections.note: Titled groups of fields. Each is a kit Section, so it brings the kit's heading row and line, takes help for the question mark beside its title, and folds away with collapsible. The screen can hold which ones are open. actions puts kit Buttons, size sm, at the end of the group's header, for things that act on that group, like Back to search or Override rate, instead of placing buttons among the fields. line thin gives the group a 1px header line instead of 2px.

actions.note: Kit Buttons at the end: secondary first, one primary last with type="submit". Size sm in a card.

error.note: A problem with the whole form, like a failed save. Shows as a danger Callout above the fields. Field problems go on the field's own error.

onSubmit.note: (data: FormData) => void. The page never reloads. Required fields must be filled first.

id.note: Lets a Button outside the form submit it, like a Modal footer Button with form={id}.

useWhen: Fields that save together, like company details or billing settings.
A settings page split into titled groups.
The body of an edit or invite Modal.
doNot: Do not invent FieldSet, FieldGroup, FieldLegend, FormSection, FormActions or a local <form> wrapper.
Do not put a Form inside another Form.
Do not put more than one primary Button in actions.
Do not wrap a single RadioGroup in a section. It already has its own legend.
Do not show field errors in error. Put them on the field.
Do not put Buttons among a section's fields, where they stretch to a field's width. Pass them as the section's actions.
a11y: A native form element, named by its title and described by its description.
Each section is a kit Section named by its heading; its description is read with it, and folding one takes its fields out of the reading order.
error is a danger Callout, announced when it appears.
Enter in a field submits. Native required checks run before onSubmit.
snippet:
<Form
  title="Company details"
  onSubmit={save}
  actions={<>
    <Button onClick={cancel}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="primary" type="submit">Save</Button>
  </>}
>
  <Input label="Company" name="company" required />
  <Input label="Billing email" name="email" type="email" />
</Form>
